headline: Steady volume. Wider reach.
lede: Comparable disclosure volume rose only slightly this month. What changed was reach: a handful of large breaches sent notices to residents in many states at once, and health-related organizations led the largest of them.

highlights.label: Comparable disclosures
highlights.context: 214 records vs. 204 in the prior 30 days

highlights.label: Organizations notifying 4+ states
highlights.context: Uber and Frontline Education each appear in 8

takeaways.summary: The full archive grew 47%, but almost all of that is new coverage, not new incidents.
takeaways.detail: Nine sources with complete records in both periods returned 214 records, up from 204. The full archive rose from 267 to 392 because DAL-X added or expanded Texas, California, New Hampshire, and CISA advisory coverage this month.

takeaways.summary: Single incidents now show up in state after state.
takeaways.detail: 23 organizations appear in at least four state breach lists in the period. Uber and Frontline Education each appear in eight. One breach produces a separate notice in each state where residents were affected, so these counts reflect reach, not separate incidents.

takeaways.lead: Health care dominates the largest notices.
takeaways.summary: Eight of the 12 largest Texas notices came from health-related organizations.
takeaways.detail: The group includes health care, dental, and medical-product organizations. The largest was DentaQuest, at 5,175,000 Texans, filed Nov 19 for a breach its Washington notice dates to May. Texas records entered the archive this month, so this is a snapshot, not a trend.

takeaways.summary: Three of the 12 reviewed national incidents involved third-party access.
takeaways.detail: Uber, the separate Chase, Visa and Mastercard vendor incidents, and Cursor each involved a vendor, service provider, or partner credential. DAL-X reviewed 12 national incidents in the period, up from 9. Five were AI agent security cases, the same as the prior period. Reviewed counts reflect editorial coverage, not incident frequency.

takeaways.summary: CISA added 34 entries to its catalog, compared with 35 before.
takeaways.detail: Cisco had 3 additions. Apache, Barracuda, Google, Ivanti, and PHP each had 2.

takeaways.summary: Fifteen of 20 recent CISA advisories covered Siemens products.
takeaways.detail: The 20 advisories were published from Nov 12 to Nov 19. The archive does not yet hold enough earlier advisory history for a 60-day comparison.

gaps: HHS shows no new hacking submissions after Oct 16 in the listing DAL-X checks, so federal health breach reporting is missing from this period. Washington and California publish only their most recent notices, so they are excluded from the comparison.
